common.browserTitle: Open SSHUI in the desktop app
common.browserBody: This page needs the SSHUI backend, which only runs inside the desktop window. Close this browser tab and use the window that opens when you run:

validation.HostNameInvalidDomain: Invalid domain name: {{value}} (must contain at least one dot)
validation.HostNameConsecutiveDots: Invalid hostname: consecutive dots not allowed
validation.HostNameLabelInvalidHyphen: Invalid hostname label: {{label}} (cannot start/end with hyphen)
validation.IdentityFileEmpty: Identity file path cannot be empty
validation.IdentityFileExpandFailed: Cannot expand ~ in identity file path

settings.title: Settings
settings.maxBackupsHelp: Older backups will be automatically deleted
settings.subtitle: Appearance, backups and application preferences
settings.confirmDeleteHelp: Ask before deleting hosts, keys and backups or restoring a backup
settings.showGithubHelp: Account, SSH access, git identity and proxy for github.com

hosts.title: SSH Hosts
hosts.subtitle: Entries from your ~/.ssh/config
hosts.emptyHint: Add a host to start managing your SSH config.

keys.title: SSH Keys
keys.noKeysFound: No SSH keys found. Generate a new key to get started.
keys.subtitle: Private keys found in ~/.ssh and ~/.ssh-at/creds

config.title: Config Editor
config.infoMessage: Directly edit your SSH config file. Changes will be validated and backed up automatically.
config.subtitle: Edit ~/.ssh/config directly

backups.title: Backups
backups.infoMessage: SSH config backups are created automatically before each save. The last {{limit}} backups are kept.
backups.restoreConfirm: Restore this backup? Current config will be backed up first.
backups.noBackupsFound: No backups found. Backups will be created automatically when you save SSH config changes.
backups.subtitle: Automatic snapshots of ~/.ssh/config
backups.restoreConfirmOverwrite: Restore this backup? This will overwrite the current SSH config.

hostDialog.fieldHostHelper: Alias name for this host (spaces are removed automatically)
hostDialog.socks5ConfigHint: Configure SOCKS5 proxy for SSH connection

adv.connectionHint: Leave a field empty to use the OpenSSH default.
adv.connectTimeoutHelper: Give up if the server doesn't answer in time
adv.serverAliveIntervalHelper: Send a keepalive every N seconds to stop idle disconnects
adv.compressionHelper: Helps on slow links; usually slower on fast networks

strictHelp.default: Not written to the config. OpenSSH asks before trusting an unknown host.
strictHelp.accept-new: Trust hosts seen for the first time, but refuse if a known host's key changes. Recommended.
strictHelp.yes: Only connect to hosts already in known_hosts.
strictHelp.ask: Ask before trusting a new host.
strictHelp.no: Never checks host keys. Leaves you open to man-in-the-middle attacks.

adv.identitiesOnlyHelper: IdentitiesOnly — don't try other agent keys first; prevents “Too many authentication failures”
adv.forwardAgentHelper: Lets the remote host use your local keys. Only enable for servers you fully trust.
adv.legacyRsaHelper: Only for old servers that reject modern algorithms. Weakens security.
adv.forwardingHint: Opened while the SSH session is connected. Listen as [bind:]port, destination as host:port.
adv.otherOptionsHint: Any other ssh_config keyword for this host.
adv.errorListen: Use port or bind:port, e.g. 8080 or 127.0.0.1:8080
adv.errorManaged: Set this in its own field
adv.fixErrors: Fix the highlighted advanced options first
adv.errorListenTaken: Another forward already listens on this port

generateKeyDialog.title: Generate SSH Key
generateKeyDialog.keyTypeHelper: Ed25519 is recommended for new keys
generateKeyDialog.fieldBitsHelper: RSA key bit length, 4096 is more secure but slower to generate
generateKeyDialog.fieldNameHelper: Keys will be saved to ~/.ssh-at/creds/ directory
generateKeyDialog.fieldPassphraseHelper: Optional passphrase to protect the key
generateKeyDialog.subtitle: Create a new key pair on this machine

hostsFile.title: Hosts File
hostsFile.subtitle: Edit the system hosts file and switch between schemes with one click
hostsFile.nameTaken: A scheme with this name already exists
hostsFile.createSubtitle: A complete hosts file you can switch to with one click
hostsFile.deleteConfirm: Delete scheme "{{name}}"? The system hosts file is not changed.
hostsFile.outOfSync: The system hosts file no longer matches the active scheme "{{name}}".
hostsFile.systemHint: Edits are written straight to the system hosts file. Administrator permission may be requested.
hostsFile.schemeHint: Using a scheme replaces the system hosts file with its content. The previous file is backed up first.
hostsFile.loadError: Failed to load the hosts file

github.subtitle: Account, SSH access, git identity and proxy for github.com
github.cliMissingHint: SSHUI signs in through the GitHub CLI (gh), so your token stays in the system keyring.
github.notSignedInHint: Sign in with your browser using a one-time code.
github.signOutConfirm: Sign out of GitHub account “{{login}}”? The GitHub CLI and git over HTTPS will stop using it.
github.gitHttpsGh: git uses your GitHub CLI login for github.com
github.gitHttpsNone: No credential helper is set for github.com; git will prompt for a password.
github.signInHint: Enter this code on the GitHub page that just opened in your browser.
github.waiting: Waiting for you to authorize in the browser…
github.hostKeyUnknown: github.com isn't in known_hosts yet. Add GitHub's published keys so the first connection doesn't need a manual check.
github.hostKeysAdded: Added {{count}} GitHub host key entries to known_hosts
github.sshTestHint: Check which account your SSH keys sign in as (ssh -T git@github.com).
github.sshDenied: GitHub rejected your SSH keys. Add a public key to your GitHub account.
github.identityHint: Author name and email for your commits (git config --global). Use the email of your GitHub account so commits are linked to you.
github.gitProxyHint: git config --global http.proxy and https.proxy. Used by git for clone, pull and push over HTTPS. Test with an empty field to check a direct connection.
github.noProxy: No proxy set — git connects directly
github.proxiesDiffer: http.proxy ({{http}}) and https.proxy ({{https}}) differ; saving sets both.
github.proxyOk: github.com reachable through the proxy ({{ms}} ms)
github.proxyUnreachable: The proxy isn't running — nothing is listening on that address
github.envProxyNone: No HTTP(S)_PROXY / ALL_PROXY environment variables set.
github.envProxyHint: Used by the GitHub CLI and curl. Change them in your system environment variables.
